title: Minimize cold-start overhead for traces and metrics in runtime
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Summary: Production services are incurring measurable cold-start and first-request latency from the observability stack. Root causes include eager OpenTelemetry SDK initialization, synchronous exporter startup work, and transient allocations from span pool miss patterns. This ticket reduces cold-start overhead and overall allocs while preserving fidelity and delivery guarantees for traces and metrics.

Goals / success criteria:
- Reduce median cold-start added latency from tracer/meter init by >= 30ms for small services (p50 cold-start reduction target).
- Reduce p50 allocation attributed to observability libraries by >= 40% in the warm path.
- No increase in dropped spans or export failures for steady-state traffic (error rate delta <= 0.1%).
- Add observability for tracer init time, export queue length, and export retry latencies so regressions are visible in Console.

Proposed approach:
1) Lazy-initialize the global TracerProvider and MeterProvider on first real instrumentation call instead of process start. Add REDWOOD_OTEL_LAZY_INIT env flag to control rollout.
2) Replace the current exporter startup path with an async background bootstrap that only opens network connections when the export queue reaches a threshold. During bootstrap the exporter will buffer up to N spans with bounded memory.
3) Introduce a small fixed-size span object pool for common span shapes used by the runtime to avoid per-span allocations for attributes and name buffers.
4) Swap histogram/summary aggregator implementations for a lower-allocation reservoir on hot paths and defer heavyweight math (percentile windows) to the metrics aggregator background task.
5) Add metric/tracing instrumentation: tracer.init_time_ms, exporter.bootstrap_time_ms, exporter.queue_len, span_alloc_bytes, spans_dropped. Populate Console dashboards and alerts.

Implementation plan (high level):
- Spike: microbench service that measures cold-start and allocs with and without lazy init (bench PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1458).
- Core change: lazy init and async exporter bootstrap (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1462).
- Allocation reduction: span pool and allocator changes (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1470).
- Metrics: add bootstrap/init telemetry and dashboard (Confluence doc: https://docs.redwood.ai/confluence/display/OBS/Tracer+Cold+Start and Dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/d/observability/tracer-coldstart).
- Rollout: dev -> canary (5%) -> canary (25%) -> all. Toggle via REDWOOD_OTEL_LAZY_INIT and runtime flag in Console rollout config.

Rollback plan: revert REDWOOD_OTEL_LAZY_INIT and set exporter to synchronous mode via feature flag. Emergency abort will apply gateway policy that forces previous OTEL jar image.

Open questions / tradeoffs:
- Thread-safety of lazy-init across forked worker models (we must ensure double-checked locking across forking model).
- Buffering policy tradeoffs: memory vs. tail-loss reduction for bursty workloads.
- Whether to upstream allocator/pool changes to the OpenTelemetry SDK or keep as Redwood runtime wrapper.

Telemetry to validate success:
- tracer.init_time_ms histogram (pre/post comparison).
- span_alloc_bytes sampled per-request.
- exporter.queue_len and spans_dropped counters.

Docs and links:
- Design note and rationale: https://docs.redwood.ai/confluence/display/OBS/Reduce+OTEL+Cold+Start
- Bench harness and raw results: https://github.com/redwood-inference/benchmarks/tree/main/otel-coldstart

2026-02-25 - Reviewer (Santiago Kim): Code review: ensure we add robust locking for forked worker models; suggested using atomic-state + mutex to avoid races. Also asked to add unit tests for exporter bootstrap failure modes.
2026-03-03 - Rohit Patel: Addressed review comments, added unit tests for bootstrap retry and failure backoff. Updated Confluence playbook with rollout steps and dashboard links.
2026-03-08 - QA (Maya Chen): Canary 5% run: no increase in exporter errors; spans_dropped remains within baseline. Observed small CPU bump (~2%) during bootstrap window. Moving to 25% canary.
2026-03-11 - Rohit Patel: 25% canary results steady. Preparing release notes and runtime flag docs. Estimated finishing remaining allocation optimizations in next PR.
